why: Chosen by the human (2026-10-15): is the recalled-vs-in-context contrast general? exp04's patching and exp02's swaps on a recalled and a bound bridge.

items.per_family: 80, a seeded sample (seed 0) of the eligible items

eligibility: B, C and O each change one token against the original (token-aligned), and the greedy continuations' first capital of the set is the bridge's (B, O) and X's (C)

counterfactuals.C: the bridge set to X, every country still in the prompt. R: the city replaced by the first city of X, in a seeded order (9000 + index), whose prompt lines up token for token; B: the queried person and X's holder swap countries
counterfactuals.O: X's and Z's holders swap countries (off the path; the answer stays)

groups.question: the question's tokens after C's changed ones (R: after the city; B: the whole question)
groups.cue: the cue phrase, from the cue word to the word before the final ' is' (the swaps' positions)

outcome: the patched greedy continuation's first capital of the set: X's capital (b), the bridge's (A), other
generation: greedy, 8 new tokens, an item's runs batched 32 at a time (Model.generate_batch: equal to single runs up to batched-kernel rounding, which changed only degenerate continuations in a check)
question: Does swapping the bridge's J-space part (exp01's probe, exp02's method) change the answer when the bridge is recalled, and when it is bound in context?
eligibility_from: the map run's items.jsonl (the same items and seeded sample, not regenerated)

swap.positions: the cue phrase (R: the city, 'is', 'located'; B: the person, 'lives'), as exp02's cue regime
swap.layers: 24-40 at once (exp02's band); a layer is skipped if I's and X's atoms are near parallel
swap.conditions: exp02's: the J-part, the full probe, the remainder, the matched-alignment direction (the J-part's cosine to the probe, the rest random); atoms I and X swapped by the coordinate clamp
swap.null: each condition's edit along seeded random directions at the edit's own norm (exp02's null)

decision.flip: per item, the swapped greedy continuation's first capital is X's; paired bootstraps over items
decision.positive_control: per family, the full probe's swap flips more often than its null (CI above 0); otherwise the probes do not move that family's bridge and its swaps are not interpreted
decision.j_space: per family, the J-part flips more often than the matched-alignment control (CI above 0): the J-space part carries the bridge (exp02's result on recalled bridges)
decision.hypothesis: supported if j_space holds in R and not in B (both positive controls passing); refuted if it holds in B; otherwise inconclusive
